## P4 contract reality / pending Owner decision — 2026-10-05

Main remains `c79659046cf6ea73ba69e03c3937d904c07ba93b`; #133 remains OPEN/unmerged at `30ed167ed57e18de0308e7ba1e0c9d0e70ab7570`. This continuation produced research and independently challenged policy proposals only. No runtime/source change, new CI run, credential value access or Production write occurred. These proposals are **PROPOSED_NOT_APPLIED**; existing acceptance criteria and gates remain in force.

`TOOLING_CONTRACT_REALITY_RESULT=NO_PASSING_CURRENT_STABLE_SUPPORTED_PATH_FOUND` (bounded to current documented mechanisms examined).

Fresh registry/documentation check still identifies stable `vercel@62.2.0`; no materially changed stable path was found. Reused same-day exact audit: 0 low / 8 moderate / 24 high / 1 critical, 33 aggregate package entries, not 33 CVEs. Active #133 remains 59.16.0 with 34 entries. Native 62.2.0 remains officially experimental; its npm wrapper cannot audit the compiled payload. SDK/documented REST still does not establish the complete reviewed prebuilt stage-without-alias flow; no private endpoint/payload was substituted.

Actual published 62.2.0 artifact inspection shows normal prebuilt deploy routing separately from build and conditional TOML config loading; installed builder dependencies still belong to the audit. **No complete startup/dynamic/per-advisory execution proof exists; vulnerable runtime reachability remains UNKNOWN.** Treat unknown paths as exposed. Bundled CLI code may escape lock-tree audit attribution. CLI tarball integrity and registry signatures were verified offline; no CLI metadata provenance attestation/gitHead or tarball SBOM was found. Whole-tree signature verification was inconclusive on Sigstore TUF fetch failure. Signatures do not establish benign code or publisher source/build provenance.

Full retained [62.2.0 audit JSON](https://github.com/markd3ng/KIRARI/blob/30ed167ed57e18de0308e7ba1e0c9d0e70ab7570/.trellis/tasks/10-04-p4-authorized-production/evidence/remediation-tooling-candidates/vercel-62.2.0.audit.json) (SHA-256 `3e4e1f11164b2d0eb96d27ceeb21c56c0659b4190359c4907ae7e84b39e8bb34`) and [exact lock](https://github.com/markd3ng/KIRARI/blob/30ed167ed57e18de0308e7ba1e0c9d0e70ab7570/.trellis/tasks/10-04-p4-authorized-production/evidence/remediation-tooling-candidates/vercel-62.2.0.package-lock.json) (SHA-256 `227f5067665298dddb3c875fabd2b5a5a091972e44680aade25888a583a6f9ab`) remain unchanged. Advisory groups include tar critical archive parsing/file smuggling, HTTP/parser issues in undici/busboy, TOML/YAML/ajv parser DoS, and regex backtracking/glob paths; full JSON enumerates GHSA IDs, affected ranges, dependency paths and severity. MAIN retained an inspectable human-readable per-advisory inventory locally; a concrete version decision must include it. No advisory is accepted here.

## Proposed Owner decision T1

STATUS=PROPOSED_NOT_APPLIED
OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED=YES
PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZATION=NO

## Exact old rule

The entire installed deployment-tooling tree, exactly matching runtime installation, must have zero moderate/high/critical package-manager findings and pass `npm audit --audit-level moderate`. No tool-specific exception is approved.

## Exact proposed new rule

For the P4 immutable prebuilt staging flow only, allow an exact pinned stable officially supported CLI release under an independently reviewed, explicitly Owner-approved per-version supply-chain risk manifest. Continue running the complete, unmodified `npm audit --audit-level moderate` and retaining its exit status and full JSON. A nonzero audit must be reported as FAIL; it can satisfy an amended deployment gate only through a separate verified Owner decision binding the exact CLI version, runtime lock hash, artifact integrity, exact Node/npm versions, runner OS/architecture/image, install mode, advisory inventory hash, reviewed command-path evidence and declared unknowns. Supply an inspectable human-readable per-advisory inventory alongside the full JSON and hash. Require a literal finite approval expiry timestamp and immediate revocation/re-review triggers; a condition-only or open-ended approval is invalid. An audit error or missing/incomplete evidence is not an accepted inventory. No version currently has that decision.

Require all installed dependencies, platform payloads, lifecycle scripts and bundled code to be inventoried as far as evidence permits; missing bundled SBOM/version attribution and unproven dynamic reachability remain explicit residual risks. Treat every UNKNOWN vulnerable path as exposed for the risk decision; command routing alone does not waive an advisory. Require independent security assessment of each actual advisory and its aggregate package paths, including installation/startup and fixed-command exposure. Pin the exact whole runtime tree without overrides, pruning, omission, severity suppression or ignored advisory lists. Verify exact tarball integrity and registry signatures; distinguish those checks from publisher source/build provenance. Retain attestations/SBOM when available; document their absence rather than fabricate equivalent assurance. An inconclusive full-tree signature verification remains UNKNOWN and must be resolved or explicitly covered in the concrete Owner manifest; a root package signature is not whole-tree verification.

Install and audit before mapping any Vercel credential. Enforce the stable JavaScript CLI path without experimental native fallback or auto-updates; use the supported Node/npm environment, a temporary home and minimal environment. Permit only the reviewed immutable `deploy --prebuilt --prod --skip-domain --yes` stage command against the exact target, followed by existing validation and explicit promotion/approved-record restoration. No build/redeploy, arbitrary command/config, guessed REST payload or general settings/env/domain operation is allowed. Preserve exact artifact bytes/provenance, protected credential admission, identity checks, replay protection, Trusted Sources, stage→validate→promote ordering and post-operation readback. T1 does not amend root/Site/Worker dependency audit gates or the existing #122 scope.

Expiry, new/changed advisories, CLI version/support status, runtime lock, Node/npm runtime, runner OS/architecture/image, install mode, platform payload, integrity or relevant code-path change immediately invalidates its risk decision and requires fresh assessment/Owner acceptance. A future release passing the existing audit should use the stricter ordinary path. Unexpected tool behavior, unsupported command semantics or identity/integrity mismatch fails closed.

## Current candidate evidence and limits

Latest stable `vercel@62.2.0` is a research candidate only, not selected or approved for #133. Its retained exact audit has 33 aggregate package entries (0 low, 8 moderate, 24 high, 1 critical), not 33 distinct CVEs. Full inventory, source paths and lock hashes are retained beside this proposal. Current active `59.16.0` still has 34 entries and the actual exact-head CI remains red.

The published 62.2.0 prebuilt deploy path routes separately from build; configuration loading imports `smol-toml` only for a present `vercel.toml`, absent in the reviewed artifact workspace. Installed framework builders and their vulnerable transitive dependencies are not shown to execute in the normal prebuilt branch. This bounded inspection does not prove absence from all startup, fallback or dynamic paths. No complete dynamic/advisory reachability proof was performed. Bundled third-party code may not appear in npm's installed dependency audit. CLI tarball integrity and root registry signature were verified; no CLI `dist.attestations`, `gitHead` or published tarball SBOM was found. Whole-tree signature audit was inconclusive on a Sigstore TUF fetch failure. Experimental native payload internals were not audited and are not a stable alternative.

## Rationale, compensating controls and residual risk

No examined current stable supported mechanism satisfies both the complete immutable stage-without-alias semantics and the unchanged whole-tree moderate gate. This is an evidence-bounded finding, not proof against all possible private provider mechanisms. T1 makes risk acceptance explicit and version-specific while retaining the complete failed audit, installed/runtime identity, independent review and Owner decision as mandatory gates. Merely disabling the audit, relabeling failure as PASS or accepting a clean wrapper does not satisfy this rule.

Pinning/integrity/signatures authenticate the downloaded artifact; they do not establish benign code, vulnerability freedom or a reproducible Vercel source/build link. Installation without credentials reduces immediate exposure but is not a persistence boundary. A temporary home/minimal environment and fixed command reduce accidental execution; they are not a runtime sandbox. Unknown/bundled or vulnerable code may execute later with the Production token, disrupt the workflow or exercise its accepted extra project capabilities. T1 and C1 therefore have coupled residual risk: one compromised executable can use the entire C1 project capability set. The Owner must explicitly accept that coupling in the concrete manifest or retain the old rule and keep #130/#99 blocked.

Approval of T1 is a policy decision only. It does not automatically approve 59.16.0, 62.2.0 or any advisory; alter code/CI; certify readiness; merge #133; configure secrets/settings; emit authorization; or permit any Production write. Any subsequent source change still requires the user-prescribed tests, exact-head CI and fresh independent code review before an engineering merge decision.

Independent security/contract reviewer (`gpt-6-luna`/`max`, read-only, not an implementer) found these bounded proposals defensible for Owner review, not gate approval. MAIN incorporated exact runner/runtime/install binding, finite expiry/review triggers and inspectable per-advisory inventory. No confirmed P4 source defect was identified.

Current exact-head [CI 37280337916](https://github.com/markd3ng/KIRARI/actions/runs/37280337916) stays **FAIL** at the deployment audit; verify/browser and actual Production Chromium evidence remain PASS. Existing exact-head code review is reused; existing independent Phase Exit Audit remains INCOMPLETE. #130/#99 stay Blocked; no new Issue, exception, audit weakening, PR commit or merge.

Official sources: [CLI deploy](https://vercel.com/docs/cli/deploy), [CLI staging flow](https://vercel.com/docs/cli/deploying-from-cli), [native announcement](https://vercel.com/changelog/experimental-native-binaries-for-vercel-cli), [npm signatures](https://docs.npmjs.com/about-registry-signatures), [npm provenance limits](https://docs.npmjs.com/generating-provenance-statements).
